subject: Airlock claim validation and evidence itinerary
messages:
From: Lara Singh <lara.singh@arborhealth.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Airlock claim: evidence needed and timeline

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. As discussed with our security and procurement teams, Arbor Health needs a compact package that validates your 'airlock' / control-plane isolation claim for Dedicated deployments. The ask is focused on network and operational evidence we can hand to our SOC2 auditor next week.

Can you confirm whether you can deliver the following by Tue 10 Jun?
- network diagram showing control-plane <-> data-plane demarcation (PDF)
- short narrative (1 page) describing the airlock enforcement model and failure/fallback behavior
- checklist mapping (spreadsheet) of controls to SIG/CAIQ items we flagged
- representative egress capture (pcap or summary) demonstrating blocked tenant-to-control-plane flows

If you can’t hit the 10th, what is a realistic date? Also please let me know if you prefer a short recorded walkthrough instead of the narrative.

Best,
Lara Singh
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Arbor Health
lar a.singh@arborhealth.com

Attachment: requested_scope_template.docx (stub)

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Lara Singh <lara.singh@arborhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Airlock claim: evidence needed and timeline

Hi Lara —

Thanks for the clear list. We can scope this and deliver a compact bundle; tentative plan below. If that works I’ll open a shared Drive folder and drop artifacts as they complete.

Proposed delivery plan:
1) By Mon 9 Jun: draft network diagram (PDF) + 1-page narrative describing enforcement points and automatic fallback behavior.
2) By Tue 10 Jun: isolation checklist mapping to SIG/CAIQ (XLSX) and an egress summary (pcap samples zipped + short explanation).
3) Wed 11 Jun: optional 30-min walkthrough recorded and uploaded (or live demo if preferred).

What we will provide explicitly:
- airlock_controlplane_network_diagram_v1.pdf (annotated; includes flow arrows and cross-connects)
- isolation_claim_checklist.xlsx (control-to-evidence mapping)
- egress-pcap-samples.zip (sample captures plus README describing capture points)
- short narrative: airlock-enforcement-onepager.md (will attach as PDF)

Kimberly and David are looped for technical sign-off — Kimberly can confirm the capture points and David will supply the checklist template.

If you prefer the walkthrough sooner, we can do Wed 11 Jun live; otherwise we’ll upload the recorded version with the bundle.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: airlock_controlplane_network_diagram_v1.pdf (stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Lara Singh <lara.singh@arborhealth.com>, ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Airlock claim: evidence needed and timeline

Lara, Ava — quick technical clarification and head's up on what we will include.

Clarifications:
- The "airlock" in our Dedicated offering is implemented as a logical control-plane tier that has no tenant egress routes; tenant workloads communicate with a narrow, audited data-plane surface. For your auditor we will supply a diagram that highlights: control-plane subnets, data-plane subnets, managed VPN/proxy endpoints, and the monitoring tap points.
- Failure behavior: if the control-plane becomes unreachable we have a read-only cache fallback for inference keys; no tenant compute is allowed to modify control-plane state. The one-pager will call out the failure modes and the policy-enforced behavior.

Evidence notes we will include:
- Annotated network diagram (PDF, high-res) with CIDR ranges redacted as requested.
- Isolation checklist mapping each SIG/CAIQ network control to the artifact (runbooks, firewall rulesets, config snippets).
- Sample pcap captures taken at the egress aggregator showing denied flows (we will sanitize and provide a README describing capture context).
- Reference links to runbooks and a short recorded demo showing a simulated failover.

Operational ask from Arbor: if you can confirm a single point of contact for the auditor (name + email), we’ll create the HubSpot ticket and the Drive folder. Also, do you want the checklist to include internal evidence IDs (we can reference internal runbook numbers) or leave them out for the external package?

—Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment: isolation_claim_checklist.xlsx (stub)

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Lara Singh <lara.singh@arborhealth.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Airlock claim: evidence needed and timeline

Thanks all — confirming deliverables and timeline from Redwood side.

We’ll aim to upload the initial diagram + narrative to the Drive link by end of day Mon 9 Jun. The checklist and pcap bundle follow Tue 10 Jun per plan.

Lara: point of contact for the auditor? If you can provide, I’ll add them to the HubSpot record and give them view access to the Drive folder only. Also note: our checklist will include internal artifact IDs; we can produce a redacted version for external distribution and an internal version with full references. Please advise which you prefer.

-David
David Kim
Lead Engineering Manager, Dedicated Deployments | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com
